scripts/partition-plan test/fixtures/alcantara-02618a9.json [--ceiling 300000]
```

The parameters come from the protected `local_review.chunked` configuration (defaults C = 450,000, S = 100,000). The earlier `max_units` and `file_ceiling` parameters, and the protected `cap` and `max_units`, bound
nothing any more (the protected configuration still accepts `cap` and `max_units` and ignores them).

### Unbounded collection

`collectLocal({..., unbounded: true})` is the collector of a chunked review: a changed file, a patch or the combined
snapshot of any size is read whole (binary evidence still fails closed), and the optional engine seed is never omitted for
size. Without the option nothing changes: one snapshot of at most 900,000 characters. The combined snapshot is reviewed in
bounded views and stored as a multi-part receipt (`docs/chunked-record.md`).

### Alcantara-shaped measurement

`scripts/measure-chunked [TABLE.json] [--ceiling N] [--shared N]` builds a synthetic
change from a table (fictional filler content of exactly the measured sizes, a real derived lockfile summary, compact
added files), partitions it, builds every unit view, merges fake finding-free unit reports, builds the thin chunked
record, signs it with an ephemeral key and verifies it through the one derivation. It prints the unit count,
per-unit sizes (view, owned, shared, manifest, foreign hunks, estimated prompt), the record size against the single-receipt
limit and the signed receipt (one file, or a multi-part receipt) size, then runs the real unit runner against a fake harness and prints the
EXACT prompt characters of every unit and integration session. No AI, network or secret is used. For `02618a9`
it gives 4 units, a 1.55M combined snapshot, a 1.70M record (59.5% of the single-receipt limit) and a largest estimated prompt of about 570K characters.
`src/chunked-measure.test.cjs` asserts these bounds and that every size which used to be refused (170 files, more than 8 units,
a record over the signing limit, roughly 500 paths, a file over 300,000 bytes, a unit over the unit budget, a file of
millions of characters, a single line of a million) is partitioned, reviewed, merged, signed and verified.

claims.description:
Add the chunked partition scheme clouseau-partition/2 behind the protected local_review.chunked.partition (1 or 2; default 1). Owner-ordered, relayed by the orchestrating session. It is one half of the chunked-review completeness fix; the other half is the local receipt hold.

Problem: under clouseau-partition/1 a chunked unit sees only its own files' sources and the patches of changed files its JavaScript imports. A unit whose file is imported by, imports, or is tested by another unit's file therefore records that file as missing. Completeness stays unresolved, and CI refuses the receipt (receipt_completeness), as happened on gaulatti/clouseau#236.

Required:
- Under /2, each unit also sees, as whole read-only sources in context_ids, the other end of every seam it is an end of, among the changed files of the same snapshot:
  - most relevant seam first;
  - read at head, or at base for a removed file;
  - only while the unit's view still fits its 900,000-character cap; an end that does not fit is skipped whole, never cut, and smaller ends are still tried.
- The context is a pure function of the snapshot and the protected parameters: no model chooses it and no session is added.

## Review partition

`src/review-partition.cjs` implements schemes `clouseau-partition/1` and `/2` (identical grouping; `/2` units also get seam
context, see "What a unit sees" above), the first stage of reviewing a change
whose complete evidence exceeds the 900,000-character snapshot budget in bounded units. It is deterministic
and model-free; `clouseau review` uses it for a change that does not fit one snapshot.

Changed files are sorted by new path (UTF-8 bytes) and grouped into atoms: a file stays with its `.test`,
`.spec` and `.stories` siblings, a test in a separate tests tree (`test_x.py`, `x_test.py`, `x.spec.ts`) stays with the one changed source named `x` (no pairing when zero or several sources carry that name), and a rename is one entry keyed by its new path. A file costs
`ceil(1.03 * (base bytes + head bytes + patch characters))`, where the patch size is the stored one (a file added whole keeps only its patch header, its body lives once in the head source). Atoms are packed next-fit, in path order, into
units of at most `unit_ceiling` (C = 450,000); an atom above C becomes its own unit. The plan digest covers the
scheme, parameters, unit membership and costs, so it is the same for any input order. Every changed path is
owned by exactly one unit (checked by `checkOwnership`).

A change is never refused for its size, and never truncated. The plan refuses only what is not a size: an
`unpartitionable_path`, an `unpartitionable_binary` (binary changes still fail closed), a duplicate path, or an
inconsistent ownership. A file with a `derived_size` (a lockfile replaced by a summary CI can recompute) costs that summary
instead of its sources. Every entry also costs `file_overhead` (512 characters, its accounting entry and manifest row), so a
thousand tiny files fill units as a few large ones do.

The number of units is unbounded (the runner executes them in waves). A stem group (a file and its tests) costing more than
`budget - shared - reserve` (900,000 - 100,000 - 240,000 = 560,000) falls apart into its files; a file costing more than that
is split into **segments** of at most C (`src/file-segments.cjs`). Every unit view stays inside the 900,000 budget.

A segment owns a contiguous run of the file's patch rows, so every changed line belongs to exactly one segment, and one
unit per segment (two segments of one file never share a unit). Its view shows that segment's patch (with sub-hunk headers
that count exactly its rows) and, as ordinary sources, the windows of the base and head text the rows touch plus 12 lines of
margin (a file added whole is stored compactly, its body once, in the head window). Windows keep the file's line structure:
the first line of a window is line `segment.start_line` of the whole source. A single line larger than a fragment (a minified
bundle) is cut into consecutive pieces owned by consecutive segments. The merge lifts every citation of a window to the same
lines of the whole source, which holds because a quote is a piece of the lines it cites, so the merged report is validated by
the unchanged validators against the complete combined snapshot. A unit's spec names its segment as
`parts: {path: {index, count}}`; `checkOwnership` and the record verifier want every index of `0..count-1` exactly once.
Inconsistent evidence (a patch that names a line outside its source) is an integrity error (`segment_inconsistent`), never a guess.

* **`clouseau-partition/1`** (the default). A unit sees its own files' base and head sources, shared context (contracts,

# Hosted chunked review

Status: dark. With `acceptance.chunked_hosted` absent (or `enabled: false`) in the protected base-branch configuration, the
hosted CI review behaves byte for byte as before, including its `evidence_budget` hold for a change above 900 KB. This
page describes what happens when a maintainer turns it on.

The tenet: Clouseau never fails a pull request because of its size. The hosted review scales by partitioning the change
into bounded units (the planner, unit views and seams of the local chunked review: `docs/chunked-runner.md`,
`docs/chunked-seams.md`), reviewing each unit with the examiner and the challenger, and integrating the seams. A cost cap
never skips evidence: when the change would exceed it, the pull request is **held** with a notice that names the cap and
how to raise it.

## Protected configuration

```json
"acceptance": {
  "examiner": "deepseek-flash", "challenger": "deepseek-v4-pro", "grader": "deepseek", "grading_model": "deepseek-flash",
  "repair_attempts": 2,
  "chunked_hosted": {"enabled": true, "max_units": 32, "max_input_tokens": 6000000}
}
```

* `enabled` (required boolean): the feature is off unless it is `true`. An invalid object is a configuration error, never
  a silent "off".
* `max_units` (default 32) and `max_input_tokens` (default 6,000,000, estimated as prompt characters divided by 4) are the
  **cost cap**. They are positive integers and may be raised as well as lowered: raising one is how a maintainer accepts the
  cost of a very large change. They live only in protected configuration read from the base branch; nothing in the pull
  request, its description or the workflow can change them.
* `force` (boolean), `params` (`{C, S}`), `concurrency`, `unit_deadline_ms`, `integration_cap`, `integration_call_seams`
  and `integration_max_seams` mean what they mean for `local_review.chunked` (`docs/local-review.md`) and may only be
  tightened below the same defaults. `force: true` reviews a change that fits one snapshot in units too (qualification).
* `partition` (`1` or `2`, default `1`) picks the partition scheme exactly as for `local_review.chunked`: under `2` every unit
  also reads the other ends of its seams (`docs/local-review.md`, "What a unit sees"), and the `max_input_tokens` estimate
  made before the run counts that context.
* Enabling it requires `grader: "deepseek"`: the chunked path grades the merged findings with the `grading_model`.

The configuration digest covers this object, so turning the feature on or off changes the digest. A record assessed under
one setting is stale under the other and is never verified by the wrong reader.

## Flow

# Chunked review record verification

Status: dark. `src/chunked-record.cjs` is called only by `reviewDecision` in `src/local-receipt.cjs`, and only for a
record that carries a `partition`. A record without one takes exactly the previous path; its receipt digest, scores and
decision are unchanged. Nothing produces a partitioned record yet (unit runner and integration are separate changes).

## Record shape (version 3)

```
snapshot      combined snapshot, of any size (it is reviewed in bounded unit views; only the views are capped)
partition     {scheme: 'clouseau-partition/1' | 'clouseau-partition/2', params: {C, S}, units: [{id, owned, context_ids, parts?, view_digest, cost}], plan_digest}
seams         controller-computed; the verifier recomputes them
result.reviews[]  {role, unit_reports: [{unit, report, drafts?}], integration: [...], drafts, grading}
result.usage[]    one entry per harness call, tagged `unit` (investigation) or by `phase` (`integration`, `grading`)
```

The merged report is derived by the injected merge function and is never stored. A review that stores `report` or
`scores` is rejected. Grades are stored once per role in `grading.decisions` (ids of the merged findings) and applied
to the derived report; the answer, its value and the set of ids must match.

## What the verifier checks, in order

1. The verifier was given protected parameters and hooks; a partitioned record is otherwise rejected.
2. A known scheme (`clouseau-partition/1` or `/2`, from `src/review-partition.cjs` `SCHEMES`) and the exact partition
   fields. Everything after this step is recomputed under the scheme the record names.
3. `partition.params` equals the protected `{C, S}` (never read from the record); any number of units.
4. The combined snapshot's digest is recomputed, whatever its size.
5. I1: every changed path is owned by exactly one unit (duplicate, unowned and foreign paths are named); a file split into
   segments (`parts: {path: {index, count}}`) is owned by one unit per segment, every index of `0..count-1` exactly once. I3: context ids
   exist. Each unit's `context_ids` equal the context recomputed for the record's scheme (empty under `/1`, the seam context
   of `src/seam-context.cjs` under `/2`). I4: each `view_digest` equals the recomputed unit view.
6. The partition recomputed from the signed snapshot and protected parameters equals the stored one, and so do the seams.
7. Per role: exactly one report per unit, each bound to its own view digest (a swapped report is refused), thin quotes
   rehydrated from the unit view, then the existing `validateInspection` against that view.
8. The merge is recomputed, grades are applied, and the existing `validateInspection` and `validateReport` run once on
   the merged report. Execution records must cover every unit, the integration pass and (with findings) grading.

The result is the same `reviews` list the non-chunked path builds. `reconcile`, `combine` and the claimed-decision
comparison then run unchanged, so there is still one decision derivation.

## Hooks and protected parameters

`options.chunked = {params: {C, S}, hooks: {partition, unitView, seams, merge}}` is accepted by
`issueReceipt`, `verifySignedRecord`, `verifyReceipt` and `reviewDecision`. Parameters come only from protected
configuration (`cap` and `max_units`, bounds of an earlier contract, are still accepted and bound nothing). The hooks are the partition and merge modules, injected so this module does not depend on them. `partition` and `unitView` take the scheme the record names (`partition({snapshot, params, scheme})`, `unitView(snapshot, unit, scheme)`); the real hooks (`chunked-wiring.cjs` `hooksFor`) recompute either scheme.
CI verifies a partitioned local receipt through `verifyReceipt`, which takes the parameters from the protected `local_review.chunked`; the controller reuses the merged reviews that verification derives, so a signed chunked review is reused with zero CI AI calls.

## Quote elision

`elideQuotes(report, snapshot)` drops `evidence[].quote` only when it equals the text regenerated from source and
coordinates; `rehydrateQuotes` is the exact inverse. A shorter or forged quote is kept and fails validation. About 90
percent of a report is quotes, so this is what keeps an alcantara-class record under the receipt limit.

## Multi-part receipts (no record is too large)

A record that fits one receipt (95 percent of the 3,000,000 byte receipt, 2,850,000 bytes) is signed as before. A larger
partitioned record is stored as consecutive byte slices of its own JSON (`src/receipt-parts.cjs`, 2,000,000 bytes each).
The signed payload then carries a **root** in place of the record: `{scheme: 'clouseau-receipt-parts/1', bytes, sha256,
parts: [{bytes, sha256}]}`, while `payload.record_digest` is the digest of the rebuilt record. The signature therefore covers
every byte of every part: a part that is altered, dropped, repeated, reordered or substituted fails the root, and the record
the verifier rebuilds is exactly the one that was signed. `issueReceipt` returns `{payload, signature, parts}` (parts as base64);
`publish` stores `clouseau-review.json` (the envelope) and `clouseau-review.part-0001`, `-0002`, ... as files of the one
immutable commit; `loadReceipt` reads them in the order the root lists, and only for an envelope that an enrolled key of the given `trust` signed (an unsigned root makes CI read nothing), and `verifyReceipt` joins them. Each file stays inside the
3,000,000 byte bound, and a receipt with parts is rejected unless its payload has a root (and the reverse).

The only remaining limit is the verifier's memory: it parses the rebuilt record as one JSON text, which JavaScript bounds at
about 512 MB, hundreds of megabytes of changed source. Reading the parts costs one request per 2 MB of record.

## Visible reasons

Every rejection is a `ChunkedRecordError` (`code: CHUNKED_RECORD`, `cause_code`: `chunked_record_invalid`) whose message is forwarded by `incomplete.classify` into the PR notice. Messages contain only
constant text, unit ids and bounded changed paths.

### When a change is chunked

The 900,000-character budget counts the whole base and head text of every changed file, plus its patch, not the size of the
diff. A change that touches a few large files is therefore chunked however small its diff: this document alone is about
87,000 characters, so a one-line edit to it costs about 180,000 characters of the budget (base text, head text and patch,
as the planner prices it), and five such files fill it. Consumers with large source or documentation files hit chunking routinely, so what a unit can
see decides whether a chunked review can approve at all.

### What a unit sees: partition schemes

Both schemes group files into the same units (above, and "Review partition" below); they differ only in the `context_ids`
each unit is reviewed with. A unit can never request a source (a request refuses the whole review), so what is not in its
view it can only record as missing coverage, which leaves `review_completeness` unresolved; CI then holds approval
(`acceptance.cjs` `approvalHold`) and refuses to reuse the receipt.

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

Status: dark. With `acceptance.chunked_hosted` absent (or `enabled: false`) in the protected base-branch configuration, the

The tenet: Clouseau never fails a pull request because of its size. The hosted review scales by partitioning the change

never skips evidence: when the change would exceed it, the pull request is **held** with a notice that names the cap and

```json

# Chunked review record verification

Status: dark. `src/chunked-record.cjs` is called only by `reviewDecision` in `src/local-receipt.cjs`, and only for a
record that carries a `partition`. A record without one takes exactly the previous path; its receipt digest, scores and
decision are unchanged. Nothing produces a partitioned record yet (unit runner and integration are separate changes).

## Record shape (version 3)

```
snapshot      combined snapshot, of any size (it is reviewed in bounded unit views; only the views are capped)
partition     {scheme: 'clouseau-partition/1', params: {C, S}, units: [{id, owned, context_ids, parts?, view_digest, cost}], plan_digest}
seams         controller-computed; the verifier recomputes them
result.reviews[]  {role, unit_reports: [{unit, report, drafts?}], integration: [...], drafts, grading}
result.usage[]    one entry per harness call, tagged `unit` (investigation) or by `phase` (`integration`, `grading`)
```

The merged report is derived by the injected merge function and is never stored. A review that stores `report` or
`scores` is rejected. Grades are stored once per role in `grading.decisions` (ids of the merged findings) and applied
to the derived report; the answer, its value and the set of ids must match.

## What the verifier checks, in order

1. The verifier was given protected parameters and hooks; a partitioned record is otherwise rejected.
2. Scheme `clouseau-partition/1` and the exact partition fields.
3. `partition.params` equals the protected `{C, S}` (never read from the record); any number of units.
4. The combined snapshot's digest is recomputed, whatever its size.
5. I1: every changed path is owned by exactly one unit (duplicate, unowned and foreign paths are named); a file split into
   segments (`parts: {path: {index, count}}`) is owned by one unit per segment, every index of `0..count-1` exactly once. I3: context ids
   exist. I4: each `view_digest` equals the recomputed unit view.
6. The partition recomputed from the signed snapshot and protected parameters equals the stored one, and so do the seams.
7. Per role: exactly one report per unit, each bound to its own view digest (a swapped report is refused), thin quotes
   rehydrated from the unit view, then the existing `validateInspection` against that view.
8. The merge is recomputed, grades are applied, and the existing `validateInspection` and `validateReport` run once on
   the merged report. Execution records must cover every unit, the integration pass and (with findings) grading.

The result is the same `reviews` list the non-chunked path builds. `reconcile`, `combine` and the claimed-decision
comparison then run unchanged, so there is still one decision derivation.

# Local review and CI receipt reuse

The canonical `skills/clouseau` skill runs Clouseau with a locally authenticated
coding harness. Installation refreshes protected public Clouseau main into one
shared user cache and registers the skill globally. Application repositories
contain their purpose and verification recipe, not copies of the review engine.

## Separate installations

Run `bash scripts/install-agent` from Clouseau, or use bastille's managed startup
bootstrap. The installer creates only a shared source cache, user-wide skill
links and the `clouseau` launcher. It creates no Actions files, provider secrets,
CI dependencies, signing credentials or branch rules. Explicit installer
`--prefix` and `--cache-root` paths support separate user profiles and isolated
installation checks without changing a home directory.

The launcher checks source freshness before every invocation. It loads an
immutable checkout for that run and preserves modified caches or unrelated
installed skills with an explicit error. An unavailable update does not silently
activate stale code. Codex and Claude Code use their existing authenticated
account stores; Clouseau makes no direct DeepSeek/Jev requests in local mode.

A run leaves no temporary directory behind. It creates `clouseau-harness-*` for a
harness call and `clouseau-wiki-index-*` for a wiki publish in the system temp

`changed_lines` coverage baseline, in the work directory
`~/.local/share/clouseau/work` (inside the CLI's state directory, created with mode

## Review partition

`src/review-partition.cjs` implements schemes `clouseau-partition/1` and `/2` (identical grouping; `/2` units also get seam
context, see "What a unit sees" above), the first stage of reviewing a change
whose complete evidence exceeds the 900,000-character snapshot budget in bounded units. It is deterministic
and model-free; `clouseau review` uses it for a change that does not fit one snapshot.

Changed files are sorted by new path (UTF-8 bytes) and grouped into atoms: a file stays with its `.test`,
`.spec` and `.stories` siblings, a test in a separate tests tree (`test_x.py`, `x_test.py`, `x.spec.ts`) stays with the one changed source named `x` (no pairing when zero or several sources carry that name), and a rename is one entry keyed by its new path. A file costs
`ceil(1.03 * (base bytes + head bytes + patch characters))`, where the patch size is the stored one (a file added whole keeps only its patch header, its body lives once in the head source). Atoms are packed next-fit, in path order, into
units of at most `unit_ceiling` (C = 450,000); an atom above C becomes its own unit. The plan digest covers the
scheme, parameters, unit membership and costs, so it is the same for any input order. Every changed path is
owned by exactly one unit (checked by `checkOwnership`).

A change is never refused for its size, and never truncated. The plan refuses only what is not a size: an
`unpartitionable_path`, an `unpartitionable_binary` (binary changes still fail closed), a duplicate path, or an
inconsistent ownership. A file with a `derived_size` (a lockfile replaced by a summary CI can recompute) costs that summary
instead of its sources. Every entry also costs `file_overhead` (512 characters, its accounting entry and manifest row), so a
thousand tiny files fill units as a few large ones do.

The number of units is unbounded (the runner executes them in waves). A stem group (a file and its tests) costing more than
`budget - shared - reserve` (900,000 - 100,000 - 240,000 = 560,000) falls apart into its files; a file costing more than that
is split into **segments** of at most C (`src/file-segments.cjs`). Every unit view stays inside the 900,000 budget.

A segment owns a contiguous run of the file's patch rows, so every changed line belongs to exactly one segment, and one

## Review partition

`src/review-partition.cjs` implements schemes `clouseau-partition/1` and `/2` (identical grouping; `/2` units also get seam
context, see "What a unit sees" above), the first stage of reviewing a change
whose complete evidence exceeds the 900,000-character snapshot budget in bounded units. It is deterministic
and model-free; `clouseau review` uses it for a change that does not fit one snapshot.

Changed files are sorted by new path (UTF-8 bytes) and grouped into atoms: a file stays with its `.test`,
`.spec` and `.stories` siblings, a test in a separate tests tree (`test_x.py`, `x_test.py`, `x.spec.ts`) stays with the one changed source named `x` (no pairing when zero or several sources carry that name), and a rename is one entry keyed by its new path. A file costs
`ceil(1.03 * (base bytes + head bytes + patch characters))`, where the patch size is the stored one (a file added whole keeps only its patch header, its body lives once in the head source). Atoms are packed next-fit, in path order, into
units of at most `unit_ceiling` (C = 450,000); an atom above C becomes its own unit. The plan digest covers the
scheme, parameters, unit membership and costs, so it is the same for any input order. Every changed path is
owned by exactly one unit (checked by `checkOwnership`).

A change is never refused for its size, and never truncated. The plan refuses only what is not a size: an
`unpartitionable_path`, an `unpartitionable_binary` (binary changes still fail closed), a duplicate path, or an
inconsistent ownership. A file with a `derived_size` (a lockfile replaced by a summary CI can recompute) costs that summary
instead of its sources. Every entry also costs `file_overhead` (512 characters, its accounting entry and manifest row), so a
thousand tiny files fill units as a few large ones do.

The number of units is unbounded (the runner executes them in waves). A stem group (a file and its tests) costing more than
`budget - shared - reserve` (900,000 - 100,000 - 240,000 = 560,000) falls apart into its files; a file costing more than that
is split into **segments** of at most C (`src/file-segments.cjs`). Every unit view stays inside the 900,000 budget.

A segment owns a contiguous run of the file's patch rows, so every changed line belongs to exactly one segment, and one
unit per segment (two segments of one file never share a unit). Its view shows that segment's patch (with sub-hunk headers
that count exactly its rows) and, as ordinary sources, the windows of the base and head text the rows touch plus 12 lines of
margin (a file added whole is stored compactly, its body once, in the head window). Windows keep the file's line structure:
the first line of a window is line `segment.start_line` of the whole source. A single line larger than a fragment (a minified
bundle) is cut into consecutive pieces owned by consecutive segments. The merge lifts every citation of a window to the same
lines of the whole source, which holds because a quote is a piece of the lines it cites, so the merged report is validated by
the unchanged validators against the complete combined snapshot. A unit's spec names its segment as
`parts: {path: {index, count}}`; `checkOwnership` and the record verifier want every index of `0..count-1` exactly once.
Inconsistent evidence (a patch that names a line outside its source) is an integrity error (`segment_inconsistent`), never a guess.

### What is reused

A review asks the harness one question at a time (each unit investigation, each integration pass, each grading round). A review
that ends `auto_approve` remembers every answer in `~/.local/share/clouseau/unit-reuse/`, under the digest of the question's
complete input. `refresh` (and `clouseau review` under the opt-in outcome keying below) lets a question take a remembered answer instead of asking again, when its input
is **byte-identical** to the remembered one except for the values that name the revision rather than describe it. The input
covers the policy and stage text, the schema, role and phase, every changed patch, every base and head source, every
source that was requested or linked, the change manifest and seams, the requirement, the prior findings, the verification
record, the configuration and policy digests, the commit ids of each file's recent history and the review semantics of the
engine (`review-semantics.cjs`). Any change to any of them is a different key and the question is asked. The excluded values,
replaced by placeholders on both sides of the comparison, are: the base and head commit ids, the snapshot and unit-view
digests, the claimed title of the change (a claim, never proof; a refresh uses the pull request's title) and, for a verification command that passed, its
output tails and output digests (its argv, exit code, coverage counters and configuration digest stay in the key; a failed
command is compared byte for byte). A reused answer is put through the same check as a fresh one against the new snapshot, and
is asked again when that check fails; the receipt is signed over the new head, base and evidence, and CI verifies it exactly
as before. In a chunked review the same holds per call (every unit, integration pass and grading round), but every unit also
sees the change manifest of the whole change (each changed path with its line counts and size), so a base movement that
changes any changed file asks every unit again, while one that touches none of them reuses all of them. The result reports
`reused_calls` and `harness_invocations` (calls actually made).

Limits to expect: a changed requirement text, policy, contract, verification command or engine semantics reuses nothing; a
verification that fails reuses nothing about its output; the store is not pruned and may be deleted at any time. See
[binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in) for letting CI keep a receipt when the base moved.

### Reusing answers in `clouseau review` (opt-in)

By default only `refresh` reads the store, and the coverage counters of the verification record are part of every key. A
base that added code anywhere changes those counters, so a later review after merging it asks every question again even
when nothing the reviewers judge has changed.

Two equivalent switches opt a review in to **outcome keying**:
- `clouseau review --reuse outcome`, for one run;
- `"review_reuse": "outcome"` in `.clouseau-local.json`, read from the base like the rest of that file, for every review
  and refresh. It is a protected control.
`--reuse` and the field accept only `"outcome"`; anything else is refused. With either switch:

Add the chunked partition scheme clouseau-partition/2 behind the protected local_review.chunked.partition (1 or 2; default 1). Owner-ordered, relayed by the orchestrating session. It is one half of the chunked-review completeness fix; the other half is the local receipt hold.

Problem: under clouseau-partition/1 a chunked unit sees only its own files' sources and the patches of changed files its JavaScript imports. A unit whose file is imported by, imports, or is tested by another unit's file therefore records that file as missing. Completeness stays unresolved, and CI refuses the receipt (receipt_completeness), as happened on gaulatti/clouseau#236.

Required:
- Under /2, each unit also sees, as whole read-only sources in context_ids, the other end of every seam it is an end of, among the changed files of the same snapshot:
  - most relevant seam first;
  - read at head, or at base for a removed file;
  - only while the unit's view still fits its 900,000-character cap; an end that does not fit is skipped whole, never cut, and smaller ends are still tried.
- The context is a pure function of the snapshot and the protected parameters: no model chooses it and no session is added.
- Both schemes group files into the same units.
- /1 is byte-identical to today: partition, views, prompts and records. A /1 record produced before /2 existed still verifies.
- The verifier recomputes the partition, the context of every unit, the views and the seams under the scheme the record names. A unit whose context_ids differ from the recomputation is refused, and so is an unknown scheme.
- Hosted chunked review honours the same setting, and its token preflight counts the context.

Classification: landing this is a mechanics change with no effect on existing consumers. Opting a repository into /2 is a review-semantics change for that repository: its unit reviewers receive the other ends of their seams, and receipts signed under /1 still verify. The docs say when a repository needs /2: when its changes are chunked and CI refuses their receipts for completeness.

Tests for each rule, docs updated, and a compatibility declaration per docs/receipt-compatibility.md.

# Hosted chunked review

Status: dark. With `acceptance.chunked_hosted` absent (or `enabled: false`) in the protected base-branch configuration, the
hosted CI review behaves byte for byte as before, including its `evidence_budget` hold for a change above 900 KB. This
page describes what happens when a maintainer turns it on.

The tenet: Clouseau never fails a pull request because of its size. The hosted review scales by partitioning the change
into bounded units (the planner, unit views and seams of the local chunked review: `docs/chunked-runner.md`,
`docs/chunked-seams.md`), reviewing each unit with the examiner and the challenger, and integrating the seams. A cost cap
never skips evidence: when the change would exceed it, the pull request is **held** with a notice that names the cap and
how to raise it.

## Protected configuration

```json
"acceptance": {
  "examiner": "deepseek-flash", "challenger": "deepseek-v4-pro", "grader": "deepseek", "grading_model": "deepseek-flash",
  "repair_attempts": 2,
  "chunked_hosted": {"enabled": true, "max_units": 32, "max_input_tokens": 6000000}
}
```

* `enabled` (required boolean): the feature is off unless it is `true`. An invalid object is a configuration error, never
  a silent "off".
* `max_units` (default 32) and `max_input_tokens` (default 6,000,000, estimated as prompt characters divided by 4) are the
  **cost cap**. They are positive integers and may be raised as well as lowered: raising one is how a maintainer accepts the
  cost of a very large change. They live only in protected configuration read from the base branch; nothing in the pull
  request, its description or the workflow can change them.
* `force` (boolean), `params` (`{C, S}`), `concurrency`, `unit_deadline_ms`, `integration_cap`, `integration_call_seams`
  and `integration_max_seams` mean what they mean for `local_review.chunked` (`docs/local-review.md`) and may only be
  tightened below the same defaults. `force: true` reviews a change that fits one snapshot in units too (qualification).
* `partition` (`1` or `2`, default `1`) picks the partition scheme exactly as for `local_review.chunked`: under `2` every unit
  also reads the other ends of its seams (`docs/local-review.md`, "What a unit sees"), and the `max_input_tokens` estimate
  made before the run counts that context.
* Enabling it requires `grader: "deepseek"`: the chunked path grades the merged findings with the `grading_model`.

The configuration digest covers this object, so turning the feature on or off changes the digest. A record assessed under
one setting is stale under the other and is never verified by the wrong reader.

## Flow

# Chunked review record verification

Status: dark. `src/chunked-record.cjs` is called only by `reviewDecision` in `src/local-receipt.cjs`, and only for a
record that carries a `partition`. A record without one takes exactly the previous path; its receipt digest, scores and
decision are unchanged. Nothing produces a partitioned record yet (unit runner and integration are separate changes).

## Record shape (version 3)

```
snapshot      combined snapshot, of any size (it is reviewed in bounded unit views; only the views are capped)
partition     {scheme: 'clouseau-partition/1' | 'clouseau-partition/2', params: {C, S}, units: [{id, owned, context_ids, parts?, view_digest, cost}], plan_digest}
seams         controller-computed; the verifier recomputes them
result.reviews[]  {role, unit_reports: [{unit, report, drafts?}], integration: [...], drafts, grading}
result.usage[]    one entry per harness call, tagged `unit` (investigation) or by `phase` (`integration`, `grading`)
```

The merged report is derived by the injected merge function and is never stored. A review that stores `report` or
`scores` is rejected. Grades are stored once per role in `grading.decisions` (ids of the merged findings) and applied
to the derived report; the answer, its value and the set of ids must match.

## What the verifier checks, in order

1. The verifier was given protected parameters and hooks; a partitioned record is otherwise rejected.
2. A known scheme (`clouseau-partition/1` or `/2`, from `src/review-partition.cjs` `SCHEMES`) and the exact partition
   fields. Everything after this step is recomputed under the scheme the record names.
3. `partition.params` equals the protected `{C, S}` (never read from the record); any number of units.
4. The combined snapshot's digest is recomputed, whatever its size.
5. I1: every changed path is owned by exactly one unit (duplicate, unowned and foreign paths are named); a file split into
   segments (`parts: {path: {index, count}}`) is owned by one unit per segment, every index of `0..count-1` exactly once. I3: context ids
   exist. Each unit's `context_ids` equal the context recomputed for the record's scheme (empty under `/1`, the seam context
   of `src/seam-context.cjs` under `/2`). I4: each `view_digest` equals the recomputed unit view.
6. The partition recomputed from the signed snapshot and protected parameters equals the stored one, and so do the seams.
7. Per role: exactly one report per unit, each bound to its own view digest (a swapped report is refused), thin quotes
   rehydrated from the unit view, then the existing `validateInspection` against that view.
8. The merge is recomputed, grades are applied, and the existing `validateInspection` and `validateReport` run once on
   the merged report. Execution records must cover every unit, the integration pass and (with findings) grading.

The result is the same `reviews` list the non-chunked path builds. `reconcile`, `combine` and the claimed-decision
comparison then run unchanged, so there is still one decision derivation.

# Chunked review unit runner

Status: live. `clouseau review` calls `src/chunked-review.cjs` through `src/chunked-wiring.cjs` whenever the change does not fit one snapshot (see `docs/local-review.md`, "Chunked local review").
`src/local-review.cjs` now exposes `investigate` and `gradeReview`, extracted unchanged from `localReview`
(an ordinary review asks the same prompts in the same order).

`chunkedReview({snapshot, plan, seams, ask, chunked, journal, scope})` runs every unit of a `clouseau-partition/1`

### When a change is chunked

The 900,000-character budget counts the whole base and head text of every changed file, plus its patch, not the size of the
diff. A change that touches a few large files is therefore chunked however small its diff: this document alone is about
87,000 characters, so a one-line edit to it costs about 180,000 characters of the budget (base text, head text and patch,
as the planner prices it), and five such files fill it. Consumers with large source or documentation files hit chunking routinely, so what a unit can
see decides whether a chunked review can approve at all.

### What a unit sees: partition schemes

Both schemes group files into the same units (above, and "Review partition" below); they differ only in the `context_ids`
each unit is reviewed with. A unit can never request a source (a request refuses the whole review), so what is not in its
view it can only record as missing coverage, which leaves `review_completeness` unresolved; CI then holds approval
(`acceptance.cjs` `approvalHold`) and refuses to reuse the receipt.

* **`clouseau-partition/1`** (the default). A unit sees its own files' base and head sources, shared context (contracts,
  the verification record, the request, unchanged sources such as the engine, within S), the change manifest (every changed
  path and its owning unit), and the patches only (`foreign_hunks`) of changed files its own JavaScript files import. It sees
  no source of another unit's changed files, so a unit whose file is imported by, imports, or is tested by another unit's
  file records that file as missing. A change to `src/policy.cjs`, `src/local-cli.cjs` and `src/acceptance-controller.cjs`
  with their tests ends with every unit listing the others as missing.
* **`clouseau-partition/2`** (`"partition": 2`). Each unit additionally sees, as whole read-only sources in `context_ids`,
  the other end of every seam it is an end of (`src/seam-context.cjs`): the changed files it imports, that import it,
  whose removed path it still imports, and the subjects or tests across a unit boundary. Ends are added most relevant seam
  first (removed import, consumed export, test subject, plain import; `src/integration-plan.cjs`), each read at head (at
  base for a file the change removes), while the unit's view still fits 900,000 characters; an end that does not fit is
  skipped whole and smaller ones are still tried, never cut. Only changed files of the same snapshot are added, never an
  unchanged caller or test (those are not collected), so the shared context of other units does not move. The unit prompt
  then says that `evidence.unit.context_ids` are other units' files to read as context, accounted for by their own units.
  The context is a pure function of the snapshot and the protected parameters: no model chooses it and no session is added.
  A unit that still lacks evidence (an unchanged caller, an end too large to fit) records it as missing, as under `/1`.
  Each unit's input grows up to the same cap, so the hosted `max_input_tokens` estimate counts the context too.

Nothing activates on merge: without `partition` every review is `/1`, exactly as before (the same partition, views,
prompts and record). Turning `/2` on is a change to the protected base-branch configuration; rollback is removing it.

**When a repository needs `/2`.** Landing the scheme is a mechanics change with no effect on existing consumers. Opting a
repository in is a review-semantics change for that repository: its unit reviewers receive the other ends of their seams

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

Status: dark. With `acceptance.chunked_hosted` absent (or `enabled: false`) in the protected base-branch configuration, the

The tenet: Clouseau never fails a pull request because of its size. The hosted review scales by partitioning the change

# Chunked review record verification

Status: dark. `src/chunked-record.cjs` is called only by `reviewDecision` in `src/local-receipt.cjs`, and only for a
record that carries a `partition`. A record without one takes exactly the previous path; its receipt digest, scores and
decision are unchanged. Nothing produces a partitioned record yet (unit runner and integration are separate changes).

## Record shape (version 3)

```
snapshot      combined snapshot, of any size (it is reviewed in bounded unit views; only the views are capped)
partition     {scheme: 'clouseau-partition/1', params: {C, S}, units: [{id, owned, context_ids, parts?, view_digest, cost}], plan_digest}
seams         controller-computed; the verifier recomputes them
result.reviews[]  {role, unit_reports: [{unit, report, drafts?}], integration: [...], drafts, grading}
result.usage[]    one entry per harness call, tagged `unit` (investigation) or by `phase` (`integration`, `grading`)
```

The merged report is derived by the injected merge function and is never stored. A review that stores `report` or
`scores` is rejected. Grades are stored once per role in `grading.decisions` (ids of the merged findings) and applied
to the derived report; the answer, its value and the set of ids must match.

## What the verifier checks, in order

1. The verifier was given protected parameters and hooks; a partitioned record is otherwise rejected.
2. Scheme `clouseau-partition/1` and the exact partition fields.
3. `partition.params` equals the protected `{C, S}` (never read from the record); any number of units.
4. The combined snapshot's digest is recomputed, whatever its size.
5. I1: every changed path is owned by exactly one unit (duplicate, unowned and foreign paths are named); a file split into
   segments (`parts: {path: {index, count}}`) is owned by one unit per segment, every index of `0..count-1` exactly once. I3: context ids
   exist. I4: each `view_digest` equals the recomputed unit view.
6. The partition recomputed from the signed snapshot and protected parameters equals the stored one, and so do the seams.
7. Per role: exactly one report per unit, each bound to its own view digest (a swapped report is refused), thin quotes
   rehydrated from the unit view, then the existing `validateInspection` against that view.
8. The merge is recomputed, grades are applied, and the existing `validateInspection` and `validateReport` run once on
   the merged report. Execution records must cover every unit, the integration pass and (with findings) grading.

The result is the same `reviews` list the non-chunked path builds. `reconcile`, `combine` and the claimed-decision
comparison then run unchanged, so there is still one decision derivation.

units of at most `unit_ceiling` (C = 450,000); an atom above C becomes its own unit. The plan digest covers the
scheme, parameters, unit membership and costs, so it is the same for any input order. Every changed path is
owned by exactly one unit (checked by `checkOwnership`).

A change is never refused for its size, and never truncated. The plan refuses only what is not a size: an
`unpartitionable_path`, an `unpartitionable_binary` (binary changes still fail closed), a duplicate path, or an
inconsistent ownership. A file with a `derived_size` (a lockfile replaced by a summary CI can recompute) costs that summary
instead of its sources. Every entry also costs `file_overhead` (512 characters, its accounting entry and manifest row), so a
thousand tiny files fill units as a few large ones do.

The number of units is unbounded (the runner executes them in waves). A stem group (a file and its tests) costing more than
`budget - shared - reserve` (900,000 - 100,000 - 240,000 = 560,000) falls apart into its files; a file costing more than that
is split into **segments** of at most C (`src/file-segments.cjs`). Every unit view stays inside the 900,000 budget.

A segment owns a contiguous run of the file's patch rows, so every changed line belongs to exactly one segment, and one
unit per segment (two segments of one file never share a unit). Its view shows that segment's patch (with sub-hunk headers
that count exactly its rows) and, as ordinary sources, the windows of the base and head text the rows touch plus 12 lines of
margin (a file added whole is stored compactly, its body once, in the head window). Windows keep the file's line structure:
